title: Colombia's Constitutional Court presents PretorIA (July 2020), an AI system to classify and search tutela rulings for selection; still in user testing in April 2021, no outcome metrics published
summary: PretorIA, presented by the Corte Constitucional on 27 July 2020 to support tutela selection (620,242 tutelas in 2019), was in user-testing in Apr 2021 (Dejusticia); no quantified outcome found.
account: On 27 July 2020 Colombia's Corte Constitucional presented PretorIA, an artificial-intelligence system meant to support the selection of tutela (constitutional protection) rulings for review, at a virtual press conference organized by Corferias, according to Ámbito Jurídico (the date used here). The court receives about 620,242 tutela files a year (more than 2,500 rulings a day); PretorIA was to group, analyze and classify them by criteria the court prioritizes, offering search, categorization (initially for health rulings) and statistics, and its developers claimed it could process rulings in under two minutes where a person needs at least a day to read 30 files. Semana (3 July 2020) reported that the program was developed by the court with the Universidad de Buenos Aires and the Universidad del Rosario, alongside the court's unanimous decision to stop receiving paper files and to accept electronic filing from 30 July 2020; in January 2020 the court's president Gloria Ortiz had described the forthcoming tool to El Tiempo under the name Prometea, the Argentine system it derives from. Dejusticia's independent research (19 April 2021, with Derechos Digitales) found PretorIA still in a testing phase with court staff, performing four functions (classification of lower-court rulings, search, non-narrative summaries and statistics) and supported by a four-person in-house AI and data team. The earlier reviewer noted that the Universidad de los Andes algorithm registry records a 2018 pilot and 2020 deployment without quantified metrics; no court statement of a verified outcome was reachable (the court's PretorIA page renders no text).
purpose: Support, without replacing, the selection of tutela rulings for Constitutional Court review by classifying, searching and summarizing incoming rulings; the claimed benefit is faster, better-informed selection.
system: PretorIA (Corte Constitucional tutela classification and search system, derived from Argentina's Prometea)
developer: Corte Constitucional de Colombia with the Universidad de Buenos Aires (IALAB, Juan Corvalán) and the Universidad del Rosario
domain: Justice administration: constitutional review case selection
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the intended good is faster triage of tutela files, and no measured outcome exists because the system was still in testing.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an attributable event; no litigant outcome is documented.
General benefit; the processing-time claim is a developer statement at launch and the system was in testing in April 2021.
General benefit; no effect on tutela selection quality or timeliness is documented.

ai_role.statement: PretorIA classifies and indexes lower-court tutela rulings for the court's selection staff; selection remains a human decision ('amplía las capacidades de conocimiento del juez, sin reemplazarlo', per Ámbito Jurídico). The only descriptions read are news reports of the court's own launch presentation and Dejusticia's research note, which states the system was still in user testing in April 2021; no court evaluation, metric or case outcome was found, and the court's PretorIA web page could not be read (JavaScript-only).

produced_by: Transfer of the Prometea approach from the Universidad de Buenos Aires to the court, with the Universidad del Rosario
Electronic filing of tutela files to the court from 30 July 2020, replacing paper
A four-person in-house AI and data-science team at the court
Classification categories defined by the court, starting with health rulings
must_hold: Rulings arriving in digital, machine-readable form
Classification accuracy acceptable to selection staff (not published)
Human selection staff using the tool's output rather than bypassing it
Continued institutional ownership after the launch partners withdrew

headline: Corte Constitucional's PretorIA remains in user testing in 2021

comparator.against: a person reading tutela files by hand to find the chamber's selection criterion
comparator.before: una persona tarda al menos un día para leer 30 expedientes
comparator.after: el sistema puede procesar las sentencias en medio digital en menos de 2 minutos
comparator.quote: Y es que mientras una persona tarda al menos un día para leer 30 expedientes y encontrar el criterio o prioridad definida por el despacho, el sistema puede procesar las sentencias en medio digital en menos de 2 minutos y arrojar las características y criterios claves de las sentencias, lo que facilitará el análisis de la información para aplicar los criterios de selección.

later.note: The only later source read, Dejusticia's post of 19 April 2021, found PretorIA still in user testing with court staff and reported no outcome; no confirmation, scaling or withdrawal was found, and the session's search budget was exhausted before a later check could be run.
